liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Me And My Uncle** (3 reviews): Phil goes wild in the break of Me And My Uncle; Phil's unusual licks gave a fresh take on a song that rarely changed [25][29][30]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the first-set Minglewood very hot; Brent's scat singing during Minglewood is not to be missed [27][33]
- **Playing In The Band** (2 reviews): Playin' and China Doll are picked as second-set highlights; The Playin' jam wanders interesting places, ending in delicate, chamber-orchestra-like melodic lines [25][28]
- **Bertha** (1 review): The show opens with Bertha, and the band plays with ferocious energy from the start [24]
- **West L.A. Fadeaway** (1 review): West L.A. Fadeaway rips [33]
- **Stagger Lee** (1 review): Jerry reaches for the high notes in the first-set Stagger Lee [27]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): After Stagger Lee, Jerry drives into Iko Iko, seemingly catching the rest of the band off guard [25]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Ramble On Rose is played well, with Jerry on form [27]

## Setlist highlights

- **Encore Keep Your Day Job**: rare: 6 archived performances [36]

## The recordings

- **gd1985-09-02.153038.akgc422.davis-holbrook.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 23 songs; 148 min [1]
- **gd1985-09-02.senn441.adam-justin-monica.ford.85981.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 23 songs; 148 min [2]
- **gd85-09-02.sbd.hinko.19475.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 153 min; rated 4.06/5 by 17 [6]. Said about its sound: Reviewer says their own audience recording of the show always sounded poor; Reviewer calls it a pretty good-sounding soundboard [32][33]
- **gd85-09-02.schoeps-oade.sacks.26077.sbeok.flacf**: source not stated; 22 songs; 153 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [21]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this audience recording fantastic [35]

## Around the show

- Crowd was small, perhaps six to eight thousand, in blistering heat, with a casual, relaxed atmosphere [32]
- Reviewer says that in decades of collecting, shows that open with Bertha have almost always been ass-kickers [24]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1985-09-02.153038.akgc422.davis-holbrook.flac1644**: taped by Executive Crew; Mike Davis, Kenny Davis, Kyle Holbrook, Tom Pinney, Olvy Johnson, Mike Yacavone; transferred by Kyle Holbrook; source: Recorder: Sony TC-D5M Location: Lawn ~175' from stage This Source: Master AUDCA Maxell MX90 No NR [1]
- **gd1985-09-02.senn441.adam-justin-monica.ford.85981.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Adam, Justin & Monica; transferred by Alex Ford; source: MAC; (FOB) Sennheiser 441s > Sony D5 > Sony D5 > 2 Maxell MX90s [2]. Also: Master audience cassettes came from Mark McCue; tape flips in both sets are patched from shnid 26077; Transfer, patching, conversion and seeding by Alex Ford, June 2007 [2]
- **gd85-09-02.sbd.hinko.19475.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD > MC > C > DAT > CD > EAC > SHN [6]. Also: Soundboard lineage: SBD to MC to C to DAT to CD to EAC to SHN, converted by Darryl Hinko [6]
- **gd85-09-02.schoeps-oade.sacks.26077.sbeok.flacf**: source: Oade Brothers Recording: Schoeps cmc441 (90deg, 17cm) > Oade M118 > Oade mod SONY PCM-F1 [21]

## Art and photos

- Poster by John Richards Grateful Dead: [1985-09-02 Zoo Amphitheater, Oklahoma City, OK, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1985-09-02-zoo-amphitheater-oklahoma-city-ok-usa/) [37]

claims.text: The show opens with Bertha, and the band plays with ferocious energy from the start
Reviewer says that in decades of collecting, shows that open with Bertha have almost always been ass-kickers
After Stagger Lee, Jerry drives into Iko Iko, seemingly catching the rest of the band off guard
Phil goes wild in the break of Me And My Uncle
Playin' and China Doll are picked as second-set highlights
Jerry reaches for the high notes in the first-set Stagger Lee
Reviewer calls the first-set Minglewood very hot
Ramble On Rose is played well, with Jerry on form
The Playin' jam wanders interesting places, ending in delicate, chamber-orchestra-like melodic lines
Hell In A Bucket is described as strong
Phil's unusual licks gave a fresh take on a song that rarely changed
Phil's unusual licks gave a fresh take on a song that rarely changed
Crowd was small, perhaps six to eight thousand, in blistering heat, with a casual, relaxed atmosphere
Reviewer says their own audience recording of the show always sounded poor
Reviewer calls it a pretty good-sounding soundboard
Brent's scat singing during Minglewood is not to be missed
West L.A. Fadeaway rips
Reviewer calls this audience recording fantastic
Master audience cassettes came from Mark McCue; tape flips in both sets are patched from shnid 26077
Transfer, patching, conversion and seeding by Alex Ford, June 2007
